diagnostic_evidence.quote: These results are consistent with those established in \cite{HL2020} and \cite{HJL2021}.

issues.failure_explanation: The introduction claims the examples demonstrate that the rates are sharp. The paper proves only upper bounds of order n^{-Gamma} (or h^gamma). It gives no lower bound, extremal example or optimality argument, and only remarks consistency with earlier rates.

failure_location.quote: Concrete examples are provided to illustrate our results and demonstrate the sharpness of the convergence rates.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Withdraw the sharpness claim, or add an example with a matching lower bound.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised optimality of the convergence rates is unsupported.
issues.title: Unsupported claim that the examples demonstrate sharpness of the rates
issues.why_classification: The fix is textual, but it withdraws an advertised property for which the source provides no support.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: v(t - \tau, x - e, y - e, z - e) \, \zeta_{\varepsilon}(\tau, e)
let $\zeta \in C^{\infty}(\mathbb{R} \times \mathbb{R}^{d})$ be a nonnegative mollifier

issues.failure_explanation: The kernel lives on R x R^d and shifts x, y and z by the same vector e, so v^eps is smoothed only in the direction (e,e,e) of R^{3d}. For v=|x-y|, v^eps=|x-y| is not smooth, so the claimed C_b^infty regularity and the derivative bounds eps^{1-2i-j} fail. The sup-error bound is also wrong: the Hölder-Lipschitz condition with |tau|^{1/2}<=eps and three shifts of size |e| gives up to 4C eps, not 2C eps.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use a full-dimensional parabolic mollifier on R x R^{3d}, normalized by eps^{-(2+3d)}. Then re-derive the sup-error and derivative estimates with corrected constants and propagate them into E_1, E_2 and the explicit constants.
issues.overall_effect: All derivative bounds for u^eps and u_h^eps used to bound E_1 and E_2 are unjustified, as is the explicit term 4C_0 eps in the error bounds.
issues.title: Mollifier smooths only along the diagonal; smoothness and estimates are false
issues.why_classification: The construction must be replaced and every explicit constant in the main bounds re-derived. The method and the rates survive.

issues.failure_explanation: u_h is piecewise constant in time with jumps of size up to C_0 h^{1/2}; e.g. for phi=|x| at x=0 the jump at t=h is h^{1/2}E|X|. Lemma uh_regularity(ii) gives only C(|t-s|^{1/2}+h^{1/2}), so (C1), which omits h^{1/2}, is false. The mollification error is O(eps+h^{1/2}), not 2C_0 eps. The proof's own derivative bound in (uh_mollifer) includes the factor (eps+h^{1/2}). The initial comparison at t=h and the final lower bound therefore miss an O(h^{1/2}) term.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 2C_0 eps by 2C_0(eps+h^{1/2}) in (uh_mollifer) and in the definition of the subsolution, and correct (C1). The h^{1/2} constant in the lower bound then increases.
issues.overall_effect: The explicit lower bound u-u_h <= 2C_0h^{1/2}+min(4C_0eps+E_1) is not established as stated.
issues.title: Mollification error of the time-discontinuous u_h ignores O(h^{1/2}) jumps
issues.why_classification: This is a local constant adjustment. The added term is of the same order as an existing one, so the method and rates are unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: Assumption (vi) provides a function l-hat_phi for each fixed phi, with no uniformity over families of phi. E_1 and E_2 contain l-hat evaluated at u_h^eps(t,x,y,.) or u^eps(t,x,y,.), so they depend on (t,x,y). The proof nevertheless treats them as constants: it adds E_1(t-h) to build a supersolution and takes sup in the comparison lemma. The supremum over (t,x,y) need not be finite or tend to zero.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Strengthen (vi) so that l-hat_phi depends on phi only through bounded derivative norms, as in the example, or define E_i with sup over (t,x,y) under such uniformity.
issues.overall_effect: The general error bounds are not well-defined functions of (eps,h), and the claimed convergence u_{1/n}(1,0,0,0) -> u(1,0,0,0) in the general setting is unsupported.
issues.title: E_1, E_2 treated as functions of (eps,h) despite non-uniform l-hat
issues.why_classification: It needs only a standard uniformity hypothesis, which the example already satisfies. The method, conclusions and rates are preserved.

issues.failure_explanation: The step |Delta|^{q_1} <= (2||D_x w||)^{q_1-delta}(||D_xz w|| h^{1/alpha}|Z|)^delta, from |Delta| <= min(a,b), requires 0 <= delta <= q_1 = 3/2. For alpha in (3/2,2), Assumption (v) allows delta in (3/2,alpha). There the exponent (3-2delta)/3 is negative and the inequality fails. The bound ||D_x u^eps||^{(3-2delta)/3}||D^2 u^eps||^{2delta/3} <= C eps^{-2delta/3} used in E_1 and E_2 also fails.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace delta by delta wedge 3/2 in Lemma consistency and downstream, using M^{3/2}_{Z_1} <= (M^delta_{Z_1})^{3/(2delta)}. This gives the weaker rate term with delta wedge 3/2, e.g. (2-alpha)/(4alpha) at delta=3/2, for alpha>3/2.
issues.overall_effect: For alpha>3/2 and delta>3/2 the consistency bound, E_1, E_2 and the rate Gamma(alpha,delta,q_0) are unproven. The stated supremum 1/(4alpha+6) of the first rate term is not attained by the argument.
issues.title: Interpolation in R_21 invalid for delta>3/2 (allowed when alpha>3/2)
issues.why_classification: The repair is contained, but the rate is weakened in the subregime alpha>3/2, delta>3/2.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \int_0^1 \hat{\mathbb{E}} \big[ \big| \partial_t \omega(t - \tau h, x + h^{\frac{1}{2}} X, y, z) - \partial_t \omega(t - \tau h, x, y, z) \big| \big]

issues.failure_explanation: R_12 is bounded by sublinear expectations of absolute differences. For the x-increment, E-hat|<partial_t D_x w, h^{1/2}X> + O(h)| is of order h^{1/2}, not h. Mean zero of X cancels the linear term only for signed expectations, so the claimed O(h) bound does not follow from the displayed inequality.

failure_location.quote: we use a second-order Taylor expansion and the assumption that $X$ is a zero-mean random variable without mean uncertainty

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Split the signed integrands by sub-additivity, without absolute values, and use E-hat[+-<a,X>]=0 for the x-term.
issues.overall_effect: The h-order time-consistency estimate (2.4) is not justified as written. With the absolute value it would only give h^{1/2}||partial_t D_x w||.
issues.title: Zero-mean cancellation applied inside an absolute value in R_12
issues.why_classification: This is a short local fix that restores the stated bound unchanged.
